name: A-level Economics (AQA 7136)
material_vintage: AQA AS and A-level Economics (7135/7136) specification, Version 1.3 (29 June 2022), the current version linked from aqa.org.uk/7136, itemised on 2026-09-27: every A-level content code at its deepest level (4.1.1.1-4.2.6.5) and the nine A-level quantitative skills (QS1-QS9). Assessment: three 2-hour papers of 80 marks each (33.3% each): Paper 1 Markets and market failure (data response, one of two contexts, 40 marks; one essay from three, 40 marks); Paper 2 National and international economy (same structure); Paper 3 Economic principles and issues (30 multiple-choice marks and a 50-mark case study). Stage tests and the mock are original questions in AQA's style; every numerical answer was computed when the course was built.
level_source: RQF Level 3 (GCE A-level), per Ofqual's register listing for AQA 7136

learner_notices.text: Economics uses real, changing data (interest rates, inflation, wages, tax rates). Where this course gives a figure, treat it as an illustration; for your exam answers, use recent data you have checked from official sources such as the ONS and the Bank of England.
Diagrams (supply and demand, cost curves, AD/AS) are described in words here. Draw each one yourself as you go: accurate, labelled diagrams earn marks in the exam.
